quote: Sandbanks, as a rule, do not exhale.
note: Verne's original plays this moment completely straight -- Captain Baker simply concludes he is dealing with 'an aquatic mammal, unknown till then.' The rewrite adds the deadpan aside, which better fits a modern narrator's voice.

quote: the serious nations -- England, America, Germany -- began to pay attention
note: In the original, Verne writes that 'grave practical countries' took the matter seriously while 'light-thinking people jested upon the phenomenon.' The Victorian-era ranking of national seriousness is quietly preserved here.

quote: Wit, as so often happens, defeated science.
note: The original goes into considerably more detail about the six-month war of words, naming specific journals like the Cosmos of the Abbe Moigno and Petermann's Mittheilungen. Most of these publications would mean nothing to a modern reader, so the rewrite condenses the passage to its punchline.

quote: the ocean, as I would later learn, does not read newspapers
note: This line replaces the original's much drier transition: 'During the first months of the year 1867 the question seemed buried, never to revive, when new facts were brought before the public.' Aronnax's foreshadowing here is a small liberty -- the original narrator doesn't editorialize at this point.

quote: Not the grinding scrape of a reef or collision -- something pointed and penetrating.
note: Verne's original is surprisingly technical about the Scotia's damage, specifying a 'rent, in the form of an isosceles triangle' and iron plates '1-3/8 inches thick.' The rewrite keeps the forensic precision but saves the geometric detail for the dry-dock examination.
